tasks.title: Backpressure and retry transient SQLite DiskFull
tasks.objective: Keep an exact failed durable output or finalize unit in the single persistence actor and retry only typed SQLite DiskFull until storage or daemon shutdown resolves the wait.
tasks.outcome: A temporary full disk no longer poisons every later Run mutation for the whole daemon incarnation, while durability ordering and bounded memory remain intact.
acceptance: Typed SQLite DiskFull remains distinguishable from all other database and persistence failures after error translation.
The actor retries the same append/finalize unit before later commands and the existing bounded channel applies PTY backpressure instead of accumulating another backlog.
Daemon shutdown can stop the retry loop without waiting for storage recovery.
Conflicting replay, corruption, invariant, file-budget, and non-DiskFull failures still latch the actor and freeze the durable cursor.
Decision 009, the architecture entrypoint, protocol text, focused owner tests, and the ordinary Gate agree on the behavior.

verification.proves: Formatting, static analysis, unit, lifecycle, protocol, SDK, and local consumer checks pass together.
Deterministic actor tests force DiskFull recovery and preserve fatal replay-conflict behavior.
The retry boundary, backpressure owner, non-goals, and old-daemon limit are explicit.
